note:
Did the posture itself become jumpier at the Sept 23 deploy, or only the token? (light: ring extracts, the checkpoint's
encoder from model.safetensors, float32 on the CPU; record section 43, WAITING 6)

    PY jitter_share.py OUT.json RING.pt [RING.pt ...]

Per body, over the lesson's window (the ring's last 6,000 moments, every 5th: 1,200 samples, 300 s): the JITTER SHARE of
a signal = its mean squared change between consecutive samples over twice its variance over the window (mean over its
numbers): 1 minus its lag-one autocorrelation at 0.25 s; 0 = smooth, 1 = consecutive samples unrelated. Read on the
posture numbers (each bone's world quaternion and wrist-relative position: the input), the velocity numbers, and the
token the checkpoint's own encoder gives (float32). If the posture's share rose at the deploy as the token's did (0.11
before, 0.40 after, the calibration's readings), the body moved differently; if only the token's rose, the encoder
answers the fast part of the input more.
